title: Runtime semantic versioning policy, LTS channel definitions, rollout gates, and upgrade tooling
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Proposal: establish a clear, operational semantic versioning policy for the Redwood inference runtime and pair it with formal LTS channels, rollout gates, and upgrade tooling to reduce upgrade friction for hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers.

Scope: runtime API surface (gRPC/HTTP), on-disk KV cache format, serialized checkpoint/adapter metadata, plugin kernel API, and public CLI/agent contracts used by Private deployments. Does NOT cover model weights or third-party model interfaces except where we define on-disk compat.

Core rules:
- Versioning scheme: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (e.g., 2.3.1).
  - MAJOR: incompatible or potentially breaking changes to public runtime APIs or on-disk formats that can cause requests to fail or KV caches to become invalid across deployments. Bump MAJOR only after consensus and a defined migration path.
  - MINOR: backwards-compatible new features, additions to APIs that preserve existing behavior, performance improvements that do not remove fields or change contract semantics. Minor releases may deprecate features but must retain runtime compatibility.
  - PATCH: bug fixes, non-behavioral performance patches, and security fixes that do not change API contracts.

Compatibility rules:
- Backwards compatibility means a client compiled/targeting runtime X.Y.* can operate against a server X.Y' where X==X' and Y' >= Y without altering request semantics or causing silent correctness regressions.
- Forward compatibility is not guaranteed between major versions. Where feasible, we will provide compatibility adapters or conversion tools for the on-disk formats.
- On-disk formats (KV cache and checkpoint metadata): treated as part of the runtime API. Any change that changes the persisted format requires at least a MINOR bump if the runtime can read old data, otherwise a MAJOR bump and a documented migration tool.

Deprecation policy:
- When deprecating an API/flag/config: mark as deprecated in docs, emit deprecation warnings in Console, and log warnings for 90 days across hosted traffic.
- Maintain deprecated behavior for at least two MINOR releases (e.g., 2.1 -> 2.3) unless security/critical correctness requires faster removal.
- For Private/Dedicated customers, schedule removal only after an upgrade window and at least one opt-in compatibility build that provides migration diagnostics.

LTS Channels and naming:
- stable: rolling stable branch (default for Hosted). Receives MINOR and PATCH releases frequently. Not guaranteed long-term API stability beyond the semver policy.
- lts-Y (e.g., lts-2026, lts-2027): year-based Long-Term Support channel. Selected MAJOR.MINOR snapshot that receives backported PATCHes and security fixes for a minimum of 18 months. Recommended for Dedicated and Private customers with strict upgrade cadence.
- compat-lts: optional channel intended for customers who need extended compatibility guarantees across minor releases within a major. Provides stricter compatibility checks and a longer deprecation window (minimum three MINOR releases).

Rollout gates and release process:
- Canary phase: automated canary across 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks at each step for latency p95, error rate, token-level correctness regression metrics. Canary runbook must list rollback thresholds.
- Rollout gates: health checks, quality regression (via eval suite), resource usage (GPU memory/peak), and compatibility matrix for Private agent versions. All gates must be green to advance automatically; failures require manual intervention and a rollback job.
- Per-customer gating: Dedicated/Private customers may opt into a staged rollout window. For Private we provide a compatibility report and an agent-based dry-run that checks config, KV cache, and plugin compatibility before applying the upgrade.

Upgrade tooling and operational work:
- rdi-upgrade (CLI): single-tool workflow to prepare, validate, and apply runtime upgrades. Features: dry-run, compatibility scan, automatic KV-cache conversion, rollback snapshot, and telemetry upload for preflight diagnostics.
- Migration artifacts: each MAJOR/MINOR release that changes on-disk or public APIs must include a migration.md, an executable migration shim when possible, and one or more test vectors demonstrating pre/post behavior.
- Private upgrade playbook: standardized docs + an automated agent that can run the compatibility scan and produce an actionable report (list of incompatible configs, deprecated flags, required agent versions).
- SDK compatibility matrix: document and publish compatibility between SDK versions and runtime versions; provide shims if necessary for 2 minor release windows.

Governance and approvals:
- Any change that requires a MAJOR bump must go through RFC, Security review (if it affects auth/KMS/audit logs), and Product signoff for customer impact.
- Minor deprecations must be approved by Release Engineering + one Product Owner.

Observability and developer signals:
- Add runtime-level telemetry: deprecation warnings, cache-format-mismatch counts, migration-failure reasons. Send aggregated counts to Console with per-release tags.
- Provide a public compat-dashboard showing supported client/agent/runtime pairings and deprecation timelines.

Fallback policies:
- During rollout, if a critical correctness regression is detected (data-corruption, KV mismatch), execute immediate rollback to previous stable release and open an incident with postmortem.
- For Hosted, automated fallback to previous runtime variant is enabled via smart routing. For Dedicated/Private, provide tooling + clear rollback steps in the playbook.

Open items / trade-offs:
- Trade-off between longer deprecation windows (less churn for customers) vs. developer agility. Proposed compromise: standard 2 minor release window, with a compat-lts option for customers needing longer stability.
- Migration cost for on-disk format changes: prefer adapter layers where performance permits; otherwise require MAJOR bump and provide conversion tooling.

Deliverables for this ticket:
- RFC drafted and circulated to Release Engineering, Infra, SDK, Product, and Support.
- Minimum viable rdi-upgrade CLI prototype with dry-run and compatibility scan (alpha).
- Compatibility dashboard design doc and telemetry spec.
- Migration template and checklist for runtime maintainers.

Acceptance criteria:
- RFC merged and approved, including LTS naming and deprecation windows documented.
- rdi-upgrade alpha runs on a Private staging cluster and detects at least two simulated incompatibilities with actionable output.
- Console shows deprecation telemetry for a synthetic run.

References and artifacts: Confluence RFC draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/rfcs/runtime-semver-draft, Draft CLI repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rdi-upgrade (WIP), Canary runbook draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/canary-runtime-upgrade

decision_log: Adopt MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH semver with MAJOR for breaking runtime/on-disk/API changes.
Deprecation period standardized at two MINOR releases; compat-lts extends to three.
LTS channels will be year-named (lts-YYYY) with 18-month support window.
